title: GitHub Trending Weekly #29: Waza, GitReverse, AutoAgent, caveman, marknative, mail-app, autoskills

sections.title: Introduction
paragraphs: Hey everyone, welcome back. This is GitHub Trending Weekly episode 29. We've got 35 projects to get through, so let's go.

sections.title: Waza
paragraphs: You dropped a claw.md in your project route and called it a day. But is your AI setup actually any good? WAZA is a collection of advanced Claude code skills from 293, known for some of the most polished open- source tools on GitHub. The flagship is Claude Health. Run it and it audits your entire AI setup across six layers. Cloud.m MD, rules, custom skills, security hooks, sub aents, and verifiers.

sections.title: AutoAgent
paragraphs: Carpathy dropped the idea of AI improving its own agent harness overnight. Auto agent is one of the cleanest implementations of that yet. Give it a task. A meta agent reads a markdown directive, inspects the harness, runs a benchmark, checks the score, modifies the code, and loops. You never touch the Python files directly. You just write program.md Docker isolated harbor compatible scordriven hill climbing.

sections.title: Research Companion
paragraphs: Most AI tools help you write the paper. This one tells you if it's worth writing. Research companion is a claude code plugin with three agents. An idea critic that stress tests your proposal and returns one verdict. Pursue, refine, or kill. A research strategist for competitive analysis. and a brainstormer built for crossfield thinking inspired by Nicholas Carini's essay on winning best paper awards. The argument research success starts with taste not effort.

paragraphs: Why use many token when few do trick? Caveman is a clawed code skill that forces the AI to communicate like a caveman. Same technical accuracy, same code output, 75% fewer output tokens. sections.title: marknative
paragraphs: browser. Markdown, HTML, DOM, screenshot. Mark Native skips all of it. It parses Markdown directly into a typed document model, runs its own layout engine, and paints each page with a native Skia canvas. No Chromium, no DOM, no headless browser. Deterministic server renderable PNG or SVG output. Default page size is 1080 by440.

sections.title: GitReverse
paragraphs: Git reverse answers the question every developer has asked looking at an impressive open- source project. What prompt would actually build this? Paste in a GitHub URL and it reverse engineers the entire codebase into a single plain language prompt. The URL trick is the clever part. Swap GitHub for Git Reverse in any repository URL and you're instantly redirected to the generated prompt for that project. sections.title: mail-app
paragraphs: surfaced what actually needs your attention? That's Exo, an open-source AI native desktop email client built with Electron, React, and TypeScript. Every incoming email gets analyzed, prioritized high, medium, low, or skip, and has a draft reply waiting before you open it.

sections.title: autoskills
paragraphs: Setting up AI agent skills for a new project used to mean hunting down the right skill packs and installing them one by one. Autoskills for Midvev collapses that to one command. Run npx autosklls. It scans your package.json and config files, detects your stack, React, Nex.js, JS, Swift UI, Spring Boot, and automatically installs the best matching AI skills from skills.sh.

sections.title: claude-howto
paragraphs: If you use Claude Code, but feel like you're only scratching the surface, this repo is for you. Claude howto by Luong NV89 is a visual example-driven guide that takes you from basic prompts to AI orchestration, copypaste templates for advanced agents, custom workflow hooks, specialized skills, and MCP servers. It even ships a self- assessment command you run directly in your terminal to find exactly which features you're missing. Composi is a Go CLI that takes

sections.title: Compozy
paragraphs: an idea and orchestrates the entire path to shipped code. Write a PRD. It converts to a text spec, breaks it into tasks and executes them concurrently across clawed code, codecs, cursor or 40 plus other agent IDE. Review comments get fetched and fix cycles run automatically. Everything lives as plain markdown in your repo. Version controlled, diffableable, human readable.

sections.title: JSON Alexander
paragraphs: Raw JSON in the browser is readable, but barely. JSON Alexander is a browser extension from West Boss that intercepts JSON endpoints and replaces them with an interactive tree viewer. Syntax highlighting, dark mode, and depth controls for collapsing massive nested objects. The standout feature is window.data. The entire payload gets exposed in the browser console automatically. So you can manipulate API responses instantly without fetch requests.

sections.title: career-ops
paragraphs: A developer automated their entire job search, submitted over 700 applications, and got hired. Career Ops is the open-source system they built. It scans career pages across 45 plus tech companies, including Stripe, Anthropic, and OpenAI. finds matching roles, rewrites your CV with 14 skill modes to fit each specific position, and generates ATS optimized PDFs via Playwright, ships with a terminal dashboard to monitor batch processing in real time. sections.title: Sheets
paragraphs: why are you still opening Excel to edit a CSV? Sheets is a terminal based spreadsheet tool written in Go, a real spreadsheet. Vim style navigation, HJKL, GG, and Gumping. Mark and jump, visual selection, copy, cut, paste, undo, redo, dot, repeat, reads and write CSV, full command mode, selledit straight from the command line. No guey, no bloat, just tabular data the way terminal people actually want it.

sections.title: apfel
paragraphs: If you're on Apple Silicon, your Mac already has a 3 billion parameter language model sitting on disk. Apple locked it behind Siri. Apple unlocks it. It's a native Swift project that wraps Apple's ondevice foundation model into a CLI tool and an OpenAI compatible HTTP server. No API keys, no cloud, no per token costs, runs entirely on your neural engine. You already own the hardware. This is just the key. sections.title: agentfiles
paragraphs: clawed code, cursor, codeex, Windex, Windsurf, different directories everywhere. Agent Files is an Obsidian plugin that pulls it all into one place. Three column view, sidebar filters by tool and type, a searchable skill list, and a markdown preview panel. Edit in place. Command S to save. Live file watching.

sections.title: boneyard
paragraphs: Skeleton screens require maintaining a parallel version of your UI that breaks every time the real layout changes. Boneyard eliminates that by dynamically mapping your actual components and generating the loading placeholders automatically. No hard-coded heights, widths, or border radi. The skeleton stays in sync with the real UI because it deres directly from it. Most

sections.title: jot
paragraphs: collaborative editors are built for humans. Jot is built for both. One command to install, one to run. Realtime editing, remote cursors, inline comment threads, configurable access levels. The interesting part, a full CLI and HTTP API, so agents can read notes, make edits, and reply to threads. The editor even generates copypaste CLI instructions to hand directly to your agent.

sections.title: rvLLM
paragraphs: Someone rewrote VLM from scratch in Rust, 12,312 tokens per second at 128 concurrent streams, 20 times faster cold start, 31 times smaller binary, three times less CPU memory, 5.6 Six times tighter P95 latency tail. No Python, no GIL, no garbage collector. A Rust native PTX kernel compiler generating fused GPU kernels up to 7.5 times faster than handwritten CUDA. Drop in OpenAI compatible API replacement.

sections.title: EmDash
paragraphs: WordPress's plug-in architecture is a 20-year-old security liability. Mdash rebuilds it from scratch in Typescript on Astro and Cloudflare. Plugins run in sandboxed worker isolates. Content is stored as structured JSON, not HTML. It ships with a built-in MCP server, so Claude or Cursor can hook directly into your site to build themes, manage the database, and write content.

sections.title: Supply Chain Monitor
paragraphs: A few days ago, a supply chain attack hit the Axios npm package. This tool caught it. Supply chain monitor from elastic polls npm and pipi in real time. Downloads new package versions, generates a diff and runs an AI agent to classify whether the changes are malicious. Automated, continuous, no human in the loop until something actually looks wrong. Open source supply chain security that actually works.

sections.title: port-whisperer
paragraphs: If you've ever typed port 3000 is already in use into Google at midnight, this one's for you. Port Whisperer is a CLI utility that shows exactly what's running on your ports with interactive menus and clean typography. Find the rogue node server, kill it, move on. No memorizing Elsoft flags, no digging through man pages.

sections.title: tuitter
paragraphs: Tutor is a full terminal UI client for X built-in TypeScript, ooth 2.0 authentication with your own developer credentials, tokens stored locally, and Kitty terminal protocol support for inline images. Browse and interact with the timeline without leaving the terminal. Nobody asked for this. Everyone who lives in a terminal will immediately understand why it exists.

It synthesizes your workspace context into a system prompt so it actually knows what the meeting is about. handles billing automatically, retrieves postmeating notes afterward. sections.title: Cabinet
paragraphs: plain markdown files on disk. No database, no vendor lockin, full gitbacked version history. Onboard a custom AI team in five questions from 20 pre-built agent templates across leadership, product, marketing, engineering, and analytics. Agents run on cron schedules. Scout Reddit every six hours, generate weekly reports on Monday.

sections.title: iron-proxy
paragraphs: Giving an AI agent terminal access is powerful. It's also kind of terrifying. Iron proxy is an egress firewall for untrusted workloads. Default deny mem proxy. Every outbound request is blocked unless you explicitly allow the domain. No accidental uploads, no data leakage, and it injects your API secrets at the network edge so the agent never sees your real keys.

sections.title: OmniVoice
paragraphs: Omnivoice is a TTS model from the K2FSA team built on a diffusion language model architecture, voice cloning, natural language voice design like female, low pitch, British accent, and autogeneration out of the box, 600 languages, zero, no cloud dependency. Inference runs at 0.25 RTF. That's 40 times faster than real time. It also handles non-verbal sounds and English pronunciation overrides via CMU dictionary notation.

sections.title: hermes-webui
paragraphs: Hermes agent is powerful but has always been a terminal first experience. Hermes web UI gives it a browser interface. Pure Python and vanillajs. Three panel layout sessions and tools on the left. Chat in the center. Workspace file browser on the right with inline syntax highlighting and drag and drop uploads. Full parody with the CLI experience accessible from your browser via a single script and SSH tunnel.

sections.title: any-buddy
paragraphs: Claude code assigns you a companion pet based on your account ID. You get what the hash gives you. No choices. Anybody lets you pick your own. Brute force searches for a salt string that produces exactly the species, rarity, eye style, and hat you want, usually under 100 milliseconds. 18 species, dragon, octopus, capy barra, and a mysterious chunk. Legendary rarity available if you're patient.

sections.title: cuLA
paragraphs: Linear attention is one of the most promising directions for long context LLMs. QLA makes it faster. Hand-tuned CUDA kernels for GLA, KDA, GDN, and Lightning Attention, targeting NVIDIA Blackwell and Hopper GPUs. KDA Forward runs 1.45x faster than Triton on Blackwell. Lightning Attention prefill hits up to 1.86x speed up. Oneline import change to drop into the Flash linear attention ecosystem.

sections.title: see-through
paragraphs: Take a single anime illustration. Get back 24 fully inpainted, semantically distinct layers with inferred drawing order. See-through is the code behind a sigraph 2026 paper. Hair, face, eyes, clothing, accessories, all separated automatically. Diffusionbased transparent layer model, fine-tuned maragold depth estimator outputs a layered PSD file.

sections.title: nothing-design-skill
paragraphs: Nothing phone has one of the most distinctive design languages in consumer tech. monochrome, typographic, industrial, dot matrix motifs, segmented progress bars that feel like instruments. Nothing design skill packages all of that into a clawed code skill. Say nothing style or run nothing design and the agent generates UI following the full system.

sections.title: three.wasm
paragraphs: The creator of 3JS just shipped 3.wazom, a 10 kilobyte web assembly binary rendering 3D at 480 plus FPS. No garbage collection pauses, no JIT warm-up, no dependencies, not even JavaScript. It spins a cube. The FAQ asks, should I migrate my production app? The answer is absolutely. Make of that what you will. Is it a serious migration path or a weekend experiment? Honestly, unclear.

sections.title: refugiOS
paragraphs: What happens when the internet goes down and you still need access to critical information? Refugeios is a portable OS that boots from a USB drive on any computer. Offline Wikipedia and Wikimemed through Keywix. Full offline maps via organic maps. A locally running AI assistant using llama file and 54 mini. An encrypted personal document vault. Zero internet required. One install script handles everything. [music]
